user.title: Set up FF Agent
user.description: One entry belongs to exactly one person. Nothing is sent to FF Agent. Next you choose what is sent with an acceptance and how the alarm reaches Home Assistant.

data_description.name: Label for this entry, for example your name.
data_description.reply_url: Open the FF Agent web UI, go to Persons > your name > section "Übung/Einsatz" (exercise/operation) > "Weblinks für Einsatzmeldung" (web links for mission reply) and copy the accept URL here. The URL only applies to you and to the currently active mission. It is a secret: anyone who has it can accept or decline on your behalf. Do not share it.

reply_settings.title: Accepting: transport and location
reply_settings.description: Home Assistant sends these values to FF Agent with every acceptance, through the button and the action. The mission reply URL from the previous step stays as it is; the values are added to each acceptance. Nothing is sent now. You can change both later under "Configure".

data_description.default_transport: Sent with every acceptance if the action does not name a transport.
data_description.location_entity: Optional: a person or device tracker whose current location is sent with every acceptance. Leave empty to send no location.

alarm_source.title: Do you use Home Assistant Cloud?
alarm_source.description:
When an alarm comes in, FF Agent has to notify your Home Assistant. The easiest way is **Home Assistant Cloud** by Nabu Casa (called Home Assistant Link from December 2026). It is a paid subscription that you can try for free first. Choose "Yes" also if you want to set it up now; you will be guided step by step.

Without Home Assistant Cloud you can use the free service **ntfy**.

You can switch later under "Reconfigure".

alarm_source_cloud.title: Do you use Home Assistant Cloud?
alarm_source_cloud.description:
Home Assistant Cloud is already active on your system. Choose "Yes" to get the address for FF Agent right away.

If you don't want to use Home Assistant Cloud for this, choose "No" to use the free service ntfy.

You can switch later under "Reconfigure".

no_cloud.title: Free alternative: ntfy
no_cloud.description:
No problem. Without Home Assistant Cloud the alarm comes through the free service **ntfy**: FF Agent sends the alarm there, and Home Assistant picks it up. Home Assistant does not have to be reachable from the internet for this. You also need the ntfy integration; the setup shows you every step.

The ntfy service sees when you are alerted, but no mission data.

If you have your own internet address for Home Assistant (advanced), you can use it instead. If a Home Assistant Cloud subscription is active, however, the setup uses the cloud address.

menu_options.cloud: Use Home Assistant Cloud after all
menu_options.own_address: I have my own internet address (advanced)

cloud_setup.title: Set up Home Assistant Cloud
cloud_setup.description:
Your Home Assistant is not reachable from the internet yet, so FF Agent cannot reach it when an alarm comes in. This is how you set up Home Assistant Cloud (called Home Assistant Link from December 2026):

1. [Open Home Assistant Cloud]({cloud_url}). The link opens the cloud page of your Home Assistant.
2. Create an account or sign in. The subscription is paid, but you can try it for free first.
3. Wait until it says "Connected". This may take a minute or two.
4. Come back to this window and choose "Check again". You then get the address and the settings for FF Agent.

**Your own internet address?** Enter it under [Settings > System > Network]({network_url}) and then choose "Check again".

Without Home Assistant Cloud you can also use the free service ntfy. With "Continue anyway" only accepting and declining work; you can add the alarm later under "Reconfigure".

menu_options.webhook_anyway: Continue anyway (accept and decline only, add the alarm later)

cloud_setup_retry.title: Not reachable yet
cloud_setup_retry.description:
Home Assistant is still only reachable in your home network. Please check:

1. Are you signed in to [Home Assistant Cloud]({cloud_url}), and is the subscription or the trial active?
2. Does it say "Connected" there? After signing in this may take a minute or two.
3. Or, with your own address: Is there an internet address starting with https under [Network]({network_url})?

Then choose "Check again". You can also take the free way through ntfy.

menu_options.webhook_anyway: Continue anyway (accept and decline only, add the alarm later)

cloud_not_connected.title: Home Assistant Cloud is not connected
cloud_not_connected.description:
Home Assistant Cloud is set up but currently not connected.

1. [Open Home Assistant Cloud]({cloud_url}).
2. Check that you are signed in and that it says "Connected".
3. Come back to this window and choose "Try again".

ntfy.title: Set up the alarm through ntfy
ntfy.description:
This is how the alarm comes through ntfy. Best open the links in a new tab and keep this window open.

**1. Add the ntfy integration:** [Add ntfy]({ntfy_setup_url}). Keep the service URL, leave username and password empty. If ntfy is already set up, open [the ntfy integration]({ntfy_integration_url}) instead and choose "Add topic".

**2. Subscribe to this topic:** Choose "Enter topic" and enter:

- Topic: `{ntfy_topic}`
- Display name: `FF Agent Alarm` (otherwise the secret topic is used as the name)

**3. Enter in FF Agent:** web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks > Add webhook:

- Type: Alarm, Webhook type: Generic webhook
- Method: GET
- URL: `{ntfy_publish_url}`
- Active: on; also for test alarms: on (for testing); also for info alarms: off; schedule: off
- Basic authentication, headers, content and query parameters: empty

**4. Choose "Done" here.** The integration then looks for the new ntfy entity.

The topic is as secret as a password. Anyone who knows it sees your alarm times and can trigger false alarms. Enter it only in the ntfy integration and in FF Agent.

menu_options.cloud: Use Home Assistant Cloud after all

ntfy_select.title: Choose the ntfy entity
ntfy_select.description:
The integration has not found the ntfy subscription for the topic `{ntfy_topic}` yet.

1. Check in the [ntfy integration]({ntfy_integration_url}) that the topic is subscribed (step 2 of the previous dialog).
2. Wait a few seconds and choose "Submit" with an empty field. The integration then searches again.
3. Or choose the entity below yourself, for example a topic you have already subscribed to.

FF Agent then needs this address with method GET: `{ntfy_publish_url}`. If you choose another topic, the next dialog shows the matching address.

data_description.ntfy_entity: The event entity of the subscribed topic. Leave empty to search again by topic.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure FF Agent
reconfigure.description:
Here you can replace the mission reply URL (for example after you regenerated it in FF Agent), switch the way the alarm comes in or create a new secret address. If you leave everything unchanged, nothing happens. Nothing is sent to FF Agent.

Saving reloads the integration; an alarm that is active at that moment is reset.

data.alarm_source: How does Home Assistant receive the alarm?

data_description.reply_url: Only fill this in if the URL has changed. Empty means unchanged. The current URL is not shown because it is a secret.
data_description.alarm_source: If you switch, the setup guides you step by step. Afterwards delete the old webhook in FF Agent.
data_description.regenerate_webhook: Creates a new address for FF Agent: a new webhook address and a new token for the direct way, a new topic for ntfy. The old address stops working; you have to enter the new one in FF Agent. Useful if the address has become known.

error.invalid_reply_url: This is not a valid mission reply URL. It contains /app2/missionreplies/ and ends with /accept or /reject.
error.ntfy_not_set_up: The ntfy integration is not set up yet. Set it up first (step 1 of the previous dialog) and then try again.
error.ntfy_entity_not_found: No ntfy subscription with this topic found. Check step 2 and try again after a few seconds, or choose the entity yourself.
error.ntfy_entity_invalid: This entity is not an enabled event entity of the ntfy integration. Choose the entity of an ntfy topic.
error.ntfy_entity_in_use: This ntfy entity is already used by another FF Agent entry. Every person needs their own topic.

abort.already_in_progress: Setup for this mission reply URL is already in progress.
abort.already_configured: FF Agent is already set up for this mission reply URL.
abort.unknown: An unexpected error occurred while creating the webhook URL. Details are in the Home Assistant log but contain no addresses. Please try again.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The configuration is saved. If something changed, the integration is reloaded.
abort.reconfigure_successful_new_webhook:
The alarm comes directly through the internet. Enter this URL for the webhook in FF Agent (web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks), or replace the current one: `{webhook_url}`

If you use the additional token, enter the header as well: name `{token_header}`, value `{token}`. While the token is required, Home Assistant rejects alarms until the header is entered in FF Agent.

The URL and the token are secrets. Enter them only in FF Agent.

If you used ntfy before, delete the webhook with the ntfy address in FF Agent.

The integration is reloaded; an alarm that is active at that moment is reset.
abort.reconfigure_successful_local:
**Saved. Accepting and declining work, but alarms do not arrive yet.** Your Home Assistant is only reachable in your home network (`{webhook_url}`), and FF Agent is on the internet.

This is how you add the alarm later:

1. Set up [Home Assistant Cloud]({cloud_url}) (called Home Assistant Link from December 2026) or enter your own internet address.
2. Open "Reconfigure" of this entry again and save. You then get the address and the settings for FF Agent.

Or choose the free way through ntfy under "Reconfigure".

If you used ntfy before, delete the webhook with the ntfy address in FF Agent. Only create the new webhook once you have the new address.

The integration is reloaded; an alarm that is active at that moment is reset.
abort.reconfigure_successful_ntfy_topic_unknow:
The alarm now comes through ntfy. The integration cannot read the topic of the chosen ntfy entity, so it shows no address. In FF Agent (web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks) enter method GET and as URL the service URL of your ntfy subscription followed by /TOPIC/trigger (TOPIC is the subscribed topic). Leave basic authentication, headers, content and query parameters empty.

Delete a previous webhook that points directly at Home Assistant in FF Agent; it no longer works.

The integration is reloaded; an alarm that is active at that moment is reset.
abort.reconfigure_successful_ntfy:
The alarm now comes through ntfy. If you created the webhook in FF Agent as shown in the previous dialog (step 3), there is nothing left to do; check it with a test alarm.

Delete a previous webhook with an older address (directly to Home Assistant or an old ntfy topic) in FF Agent; it no longer works.

The integration is reloaded; an alarm that is active at that moment is reset.
abort.reconfigure_successful_ntfy_other_addres:
The alarm now comes through ntfy. **Note: The address differs from the previous dialog**, because the chosen entity uses another topic or another ntfy server. Enter this address in FF Agent (web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks): method GET, URL `{ntfy_publish_url}`, basic authentication, headers, content and query parameters empty.

Delete a previous webhook that points directly at Home Assistant in FF Agent; it no longer works.

The URL contains your secret topic. Enter it only in FF Agent.

The integration is reloaded; an alarm that is active at that moment is reset.

create_entry.cloud:
Done: Home Assistant is reachable through Home Assistant Cloud. Now just set up FF Agent:

1. Open FF Agent in the browser: web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks > Add webhook.
2. Type: Alarm, Webhook type: Generic webhook.
3. Method: POST.
4. URL: `{webhook_url}`
5. Active: on; also for test alarms: on (for testing; automations then also run for test alarms); also for info alarms: off; schedule enabled: off.
6. Leave basic authentication, content and query parameters empty, save.
7. Check with a test alarm: "Alarm active" turns on in Home Assistant.

The URL is a secret. Enter it only in FF Agent.
create_entry.external:
Done: Home Assistant is reachable through your own internet address. Now just set up FF Agent:

1. Open FF Agent in the browser: web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks > Add webhook.
2. Type: Alarm, Webhook type: Generic webhook.
3. Method: POST.
4. URL: `{webhook_url}`
5. Active: on; also for test alarms: on (for testing; automations then also run for test alarms); also for info alarms: off; schedule enabled: off.
6. Leave basic authentication, content and query parameters empty, save.
7. Check with a test alarm: "Alarm active" turns on in Home Assistant.

The URL is a secret. Enter it only in FF Agent.
create_entry.internal:
**Saved. Accepting and declining work, but alarms do not arrive yet.** Your Home Assistant is only reachable in your home network (`{webhook_url}`), and FF Agent is on the internet.

This is how you add the alarm later:

1. Set up [Home Assistant Cloud]({cloud_url}) (called Home Assistant Link from December 2026) or enter your own internet address.
2. Open "Reconfigure" of this entry and save. You then get the address and the settings for FF Agent.

Or choose the free way through ntfy under "Reconfigure".

Only create the webhook in FF Agent once you have the new address.
create_entry.path_only:
**Saved. Accepting and declining work, but alarms do not arrive yet.** Home Assistant does not know an address of its own yet, only the path `{webhook_url}`, and FF Agent is on the internet.

This is how you add the alarm later:

1. Set up [Home Assistant Cloud]({cloud_url}) (called Home Assistant Link from December 2026) or enter your own internet address.
2. Open "Reconfigure" of this entry and save. You then get the address and the settings for FF Agent.

Or choose the free way through ntfy under "Reconfigure".

Only create the webhook in FF Agent once you have the new address.
create_entry.ntfy_topic_unknown:
Done: The ntfy entity has been chosen, the setup is complete.

The integration cannot read the topic of this ntfy entity, so it shows no address. Create a webhook in FF Agent (web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks):

- Type: Alarm
- Webhook type: Generic webhook
- Method: GET
- URL: the service URL of your ntfy subscription followed by /TOPIC/trigger (TOPIC is the subscribed topic)
- Active: on; schedule enabled: off
- Basic authentication, headers, content and query parameters: empty

The topic is a secret. Enter the URL only in FF Agent.
create_entry.ntfy:
Done: The ntfy entity has been found, the setup is complete.

If you created the webhook in FF Agent as shown in the previous dialog (step 3), there is nothing left to do. Check the chain with a test alarm: "Alarm active" turns on in Home Assistant. You can look up the values for FF Agent at any time under "Configure".

**Good to know:** The ntfy service sees when you are alerted, but no mission data. If Home Assistant or the internet connection is down when an alarm comes in, the alarm is lost, because ntfy does not deliver it later.
create_entry.ntfy_other_address:
Done: The ntfy entity has been chosen, the setup is complete.

**Note: The address for FF Agent differs from the previous dialog**, because the chosen entity uses another topic or another ntfy server. Create or correct the webhook in FF Agent (web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks) with these values:

- Type: Alarm
- Webhook type: Generic webhook
- Method: GET
- URL: `{ntfy_publish_url}`
- Active: on
- Also for test alarms: on (for testing; automations then also run for test alarms)
- Also for info alarms: off
- Schedule enabled: off
- Basic authentication, headers, content and query parameters: empty

The URL contains your secret topic. Enter it only in FF Agent.

Then check with a test alarm that "Alarm active" turns on.

**Good to know:** The ntfy service sees when you are alerted, but no mission data. If Home Assistant or the internet connection is down when an alarm comes in, the alarm is lost, because ntfy does not deliver it later.

init.title: FF Agent: Options
init.description:
**Webhook access for FF Agent**

- URL: `{webhook_url}`
- Kind of address: `{url_kind}` (cloud = Home Assistant Cloud, external = own internet address, internal = internal only, path_only = path only)
- Header name: `{token_header}`
- Token: `{token}`

In FF Agent (web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks) use these values: Type Alarm, Webhook type Generic webhook, Method POST, the URL from above, Active on, Schedule off, Basic authentication, content and query parameters empty. You only need the header with the token if "Require additional token" below is on.

If the kind above is `internal` or `path_only`, FF Agent cannot reach the address. Set up [Home Assistant Cloud]({cloud_url}) and then open "Reconfigure", or switch to the free way through ntfy there.

The URL and the token are secrets. Do not share them or screenshots of this page.

**Saving reloads the integration; an alarm that is active at that moment is reset.**

data_description.require_token: Only turn this on once the header is entered in FF Agent and a test alarm shows `x-ff-agent-token` under `header_names` in the diagnostics. Recommended if automations control gates or doors. Calls without a valid token are rejected then.
data_description.reset_minutes: Minutes without a new alarm after which "Alarm active" turns off again (1 to 1440).
data_description.default_transport: Sent with an acceptance if the action does not name a transport.
data_description.location_entity: Optional: a person or device tracker whose location is sent with an acceptance. Leave empty to send no location.

ntfy.title: FF Agent: Options
ntfy.description:
**Alarm through ntfy**

- Entity: `{ntfy_entity}`
- Address for FF Agent: `{ntfy_publish_url}` (method GET)

In FF Agent (web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks) use these values: Type Alarm, Webhook type Generic webhook, Method GET, the address from above, Active on, Schedule off, basic authentication, headers, content and query parameters empty.

There is no additional token with ntfy. The topic in the address is the only protection: do not share it or screenshots of this page. You change the way, the entity or the topic under "Reconfigure".

**Saving reloads the integration; an alarm that is active at that moment is reset.**

data_description.reset_minutes: Minutes without a new alarm after which "Alarm active" turns off again (1 to 1440).
data_description.default_transport: Sent with an acceptance if the action does not name a transport.
data_description.location_entity: Optional: a person or device tracker whose location is sent with an acceptance. Leave empty to send no location.

reply_connection_error.message: FF Agent could not be reached or did not answer in time. The reply was probably not sent. Check the internet connection and try again.

reply_http_error.message: FF Agent answered with HTTP status {status}. The reply was probably not recorded. Check in FF Agent whether a reply is possible for the current mission.

invalid_transport.message: The mode of transport "{transport}" is not supported. Supported are car, feet (on foot) and bicycle.

options.webhook: Through Home Assistant Cloud or your own internet address (recommended). Requires a Home Assistant Cloud subscription or an address of your Home Assistant that is reachable from the internet (IP address or domain).
options.ntfy: Through the free service ntfy. No subscription needed, Home Assistant does not have to be reachable from the internet.

accept.name: Accept
accept.description: Accepts the current mission for one person. Without a mode of transport the default of the entry is used; a location is only sent if you enter it here or set a location entity in the options.

config_entry_id.name: Entry
config_entry_id.description: The FF Agent entry of the person who accepts.

transport.name: Mode of transport
transport.description: How the person gets to the mission: by car, on foot or by bicycle.

latitude.name: Latitude
latitude.description: Latitude of the current location. Needs the longitude as well. Leave both empty to send no location.

longitude.name: Longitude
longitude.description: Longitude of the current location. Needs the latitude as well.

reject.name: Decline
reject.description: Declines the current mission for one person.

config_entry_id.name: Entry
config_entry_id.description: The FF Agent entry of the person who declines.

webhook_token_rejected.title: FF Agent webhook call rejected
webhook_token_rejected.description:
A call to the FF Agent webhook of "{title}" was rejected because the header X-FF-Agent-Token was missing or wrong. An alarm may have been lost.

Check in FF Agent (web UI > Automation > Personal webhooks) that the header X-FF-Agent-Token with the token of this entry is set. If you use Home Assistant Cloud (Nabu Casa) and the header does not arrive, switch off the option to require the additional token in the options of this entry.

This notice disappears with the next accepted call.

ntfy_entity_missing.title: FF Agent: ntfy subscription for the alarm is missing
ntfy_entity_missing.description:
The entry "{title}" receives alarms through ntfy but cannot find the ntfy entity anymore, or it is disabled. Until then no alarms arrive; accepting and declining still work.

Subscribe to the same topic in the ntfy integration again, or choose an existing ntfy entity or the direct way through the internet under "Reconfigure" of this entry.

The entry adopts a new subscription of the same topic by itself, then this notice disappears. If the notice stays: choose the new entity under "Reconfigure".
